results.headline: Employer of record first, then your own company from month 7
results.reason: Your own company becomes cheaper to run once you reach about 6 people, around month 7.
results.money: Saves about €58,180 over 24 months compared with employer of record, on top of pay.
notes: People who work only for you under your direction are usually employees, so contractors are not a safe option.
You plan a permanent presence, which also points to your own company.
Running your own company costs 30% more here because you do not work in the local language.
steps: Month 3: hire your first 3 people through employer of record.
Month 4: start setting up your GmbH. It usually takes 6 to 12 weeks.
Month 7: move your team onto your own company.
flags: In Germany an employer of record must hold a labour leasing licence, and the same person can usually be placed with you for at most 18 months.

review.summary: The recommended route is to hire through an employer of record from month 3, then move the team onto your own German company (GmbH) from month 7. This saves about €58,180 over 24 months compared with staying on an employer of record, because the cost on top of pay is €71,085 on the recommended plan against €129,265 if you stay.
review.driver: All three checks point towards your own company: financial, strategic and risk, giving a score of 3. The team reaches about six people around month 7, which is when running your own company becomes cheaper than paying an employer of record's fee, and the permanent presence you plan also favours your own company.
risks: The GmbH setup usually takes 6 to 12 weeks, so starting in month 4 leaves little margin to be ready by the month 7 deadline. A delay would keep the team on the more expensive employer of record route for longer.

The risk check points towards your own company, yet none of the specific risk triggers (sales, manager, licences or regulated activity) was reported. The reason for this check should be understood before committing.

Running your own company costs 30% more because you do not work in the local language, and the running cost of €2,600 a month depends on this uplift. Any change in headcount or cost assumptions could move the crossover point.
confirm: Can a German GmbH realistically be registered, with bank account, payroll registration and social security set up, within the window from month 4 to month 7?
Are the three to five people who work only under your direction employees in Germany, and does the employer of record's labour leasing licence cover them for the planned months?
